The FIXME fires for HeapCompatibilityInformation values other than 0 or 2, and Wine returns STATUS_UNSUCCESSFUL for them. kernel32/tests/heap.c:873-876 ok(!ret) and ok(GetLastError()==ERROR_GEN_FAILURE) for compat_info=1. learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/heapapi/nf-heapapi-heapsetinformation: "Only the low-fragmentation heap (LFH) is supported". Only the FIXME level is wrong: make it WARN.

[apps: pdn2, vscode] ThreadPriority (absolute 1..31, ZwSetInformationThread docs: "must be > LOW_PRIORITY and <= HIGH_PRIORITY") cannot be stored: the server keeps only the relative Win32 priorities (server/thread.c:628-640 accepts -2..2, IDLE and TIME_CRITICAL outside the realtime class). Proposal: keep an absolute dynamic priority per thread in the server, mapped to the nice/RT value Wine already derives, and report it in ThreadBasicInformation. Design decision for the scheduler model

(apps by import only, logs=0) The FIXME at file.c:8663 fires only if the server's ObjectTypesInformation reply overflows a client buffer sized for 32 types of 16 chars. server/directory.c:142-166 registers 22 types, so the reply (about 22*(36+40) bytes) always fits: the branch is unreachable in this tree. Real gap, no test: win32u/message.c:1240-1244 pack_message fails (count=-1) any cross-process WM_NCPAINT whose wParam is an HRGN (>1); dce.c:1751 itself sends WM_NCPAINT(whole_rgn), so cross-process child/embedded windows lose NC paint. Design proposal: pass handle-only wParams through unmarshalled; for WM_NCPAINT the receiver cannot use another process's HRGN, so pack it as wParam=1 (whole frame) or have the server send the region as rect data and recreate it on unpack.

(apps hit: vscode/libuv) FILE_DISPOSITION_FORCE_IMAGE_SECTION_CHECK asks for the mapped-image check. Our server already always refuses deletion while any mapping exists: server/fd.c:2873-2879 returns STATUS_CANNOT_DELETE if any open fd has FILE_MAPPING_ACCESS. WDK ntddk/ns-ntddk-_file_disposition_information_ex: "A return value of STATUS_CANNOT_DELETE indicates that either the file is read-only, or there is an existing mapped view to the file." The flag's effect is therefore already in place; make the FIXME (file.c:5700) a TRACE.

Privileges/LSA. Returns STATUS_SUCCESS without granting anything (fake success). Proposal: Windows stores account rights in the LSA policy DB; require POLICY_CREATE_ACCOUNT|POLICY_LOOKUP_NAMES on the handle (admin) else STATUS_ACCESS_DENIED; validate names against the privilege/right list (STATUS_NO_SUCH_PRIVILEGE); persist per-SID rights (wineserver-held policy store, e.g. HKLM\SECURITY\Policy\Accounts\<SID>) and have token creation (LogonUser/broker) add those privileges to new tokens. Must be paired with 70/72/81.

ACLs. W returns 1 (ERROR_INVALID_FUNCTION) and never writes *pAccessRights. Proposal (Windows algorithm per learn GetEffectiveRightsFromAclW): resolve trustee to SID (trustee_to_sid); if trustee is a user, also its groups (for the current user use token groups; otherwise Everyone/Authenticated Users/local groups via NetUserGetLocalGroups); walk ACEs in order, accumulating ACCESS_ALLOWED bits not already denied, skipping INHERIT_ONLY ACEs; NULL ACL -> all rights; return ERROR_SUCCESS.

(b) Doc https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/combaseapi/nf-combaseapi-cogetcallertid: lpdwTID = caller apartment ID (STA thread id, 0 for MTA, -1 for NA); S_TRUE same process, S_FALSE other process. Wine never transmits the caller apartment over ORPC, so this needs a wire/channel design. Proposal: record caller tid/apt type and pid in the per-call message_state (same-process calls) and in a Wine-private ORPC extent for cross-process calls; on server dispatch store it in tlsdata so CoGetCallerTID reads it; outside a call return the documented failure.

[apps: 1] Forwards to SetWaitableTimer and ignores WakeContext/TolerableDelay. https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/synchapi/nf-synchapi-setwaitabletimerex: 'similar to the SetWaitableTimer function, except SetWaitableTimerEx can be used to specify a context string and a tolerable delay'. TolerableDelay is a coalescing allowance (firing on time is valid), and WakeContext is diagnostic for wake timers. Gap: resume is hard-coded FALSE, which matches Ex having no fResume parameter. Only cosmetic: drop the FIXME.

Logon sessions. apps hit it (vscode). Returns 0 sessions (Windows always has at least SYSTEM 0x3e7, NetworkService 0x3e4, LocalService 0x3e5 and the interactive user's). Proposal: wineserver enumerates logon-session LUIDs of live tokens (AuthenticationId) and returns them in an LsaFreeReturnBuffer-able array; non-admin callers see only sessions they may query (Windows: needs SeTcbPrivilege/admin for others' sessions).

Real gap (firefox hits it): imm32/tests/imm32.c:3725-3727 has todo_wine ok(ret,"UnloadKeyboardLayout failed"). Proposal: keep a per-session list of loaded HKLs in win32u/wineserver. LoadKeyboardLayout* adds to it, Unload removes (fails if it is the active or last layout), GetKeyboardLayoutList returns it.

SECURITY (code signing): SetCachedSigningLevel returns TRUE and caches nothing (security.c:1641). Proposal: Wine has no Code Integrity/signing-level cache, so do not claim success. Fail with ERROR_NOT_SUPPORTED (or validate the file handle and return the CI-unavailable status) until a signing-level store exists, e.g. NtSetCachedSigningLevel backed by an Authenticode check via wintrust plus an EA/xattr cache. Keep GetCachedSigningLevel consistent with it.

Logon sessions. apps hit it (vscode). Semi-stub: only LogonId and AuthenticationPackage are filled for ANY LUID. Proposal: look up the logon session by LUID (wineserver token AuthenticationId); fill UserName, LogonDomain, Sid, LogonType (Interactive=2 for the desktop user, Service=5 for 0x3e7 etc), Session, LogonTime, LogonServer, DnsDomainName, Upn as Windows does; unknown LUID -> STATUS_NO_SUCH_LOGON_SESSION; other users' sessions require admin/SeTcbPrivilege else STATUS_ACCESS_DENIED.

LSA policy (security model). Trusted domains. Returns STATUS_SUCCESS without creating a trust or handle (fake success; *domain unset). Proposal: a workstation (not a DC) cannot create trusts: return STATUS_DIRECTORY_SERVICE_REQUIRED / STATUS_INVALID_DOMAIN_ROLE after checking POLICY_TRUST_ADMIN access (STATUS_ACCESS_DENIED for non-admins); never succeed.

LSA policy (security model). Trusted domains. Returns STATUS_SUCCESS deleting nothing. Proposal: no trusts exist on a standalone workstation: check POLICY_TRUST_ADMIN (STATUS_ACCESS_DENIED), then STATUS_OBJECT_NAME_NOT_FOUND.

Privileges/LSA. advapi32/tests/lsa.c:173-177 ok() accepts STATUS_SUCCESS or STATUS_OBJECT_NAME_NOT_FOUND (rights=NULL,count=0 on failure), so current output passes, but a SID with rights (Administrators: SeBackupPrivilege, SeDebugPrivilege...) gets none. Proposal: read the per-SID rights store (same as 28) seeded with Windows' default User Rights Assignment for Administrators/Users/Everyone/LocalService/NetworkService/SYSTEM; requires POLICY_LOOKUP_NAMES.

LSA policy (security model). Accounts. Returns STATUS_NO_MORE_ENTRIES. Proposal: enumerate SIDs that have an LSA account object (those with any right in the store of 28, Windows default set) as LSA_ENUMERATION_INFORMATION array with resumable context, needs POLICY_VIEW_LOCAL_INFORMATION.

Privileges/LSA. Returns STATUS_NO_MORE_ENTRIES (and leaves *buffer/*count unset). Proposal: from the rights store (28) return LSA_ENUMERATION_INFORMATION for SIDs holding the right (e.g. SeServiceLogonRight, SeDebugPrivilege -> Administrators), STATUS_NO_SUCH_PRIVILEGE for unknown names, STATUS_NO_MORE_ENTRIES if none; requires POLICY_LOOKUP_NAMES|POLICY_VIEW_LOCAL_INFORMATION (admin).

LSA policy (security model). Trusted domains. Returns STATUS_SUCCESS with count 0 and *Buffer unset. Proposal: standalone workstation has no trusts: require POLICY_VIEW_LOCAL_INFORMATION, set *Buffer=NULL, *count=0 and return STATUS_NO_MORE_ENTRIES (end of enumeration), never leave Buffer uninitialised.
LSA policy (security model). Same as 73 for the Ex form: *buffer=NULL, *count=0, STATUS_NO_MORE_ENTRIES after access check.

LSA policy (security model). Name lookup. LsaLookupNames returns STATUS_NONE_MAPPED for everything while LsaLookupNames2 is implemented in the same file (lookup_name helper). Proposal: implement LsaLookupNames as LsaLookupNames2(flags 0) and convert LSA_TRANSLATED_SID2 -> LSA_TRANSLATED_SID (RelativeId = last subauthority, DomainIndex), same STATUS_SOME_NOT_MAPPED/NONE_MAPPED rules.

LSA policy (security model). Trusted domains. Returns STATUS_OBJECT_NAME_NOT_FOUND, which is what a standalone workstation reports (no trusts); keep it, but add the POLICY access check (STATUS_ACCESS_DENIED) and set *handle=NULL.

LSA policy (security model). Classes PolicyAuditLog/PdAccount/LsaServerRole/ReplicaSource/DefaultQuota/Modification/AuditFull* fall to FIXME. Proposal (Windows workstation values): PolicyLsaServerRoleInformation -> PolicyServerRolePrimary; PolicyPdAccountInformation -> empty Name; PolicyAuditLogInformation -> retention/size from the Security event log config; PolicyModificationInformation -> ModifiedId + DatabaseCreationTime from the store; PolicyDefaultQuotaInformation -> default QUOTA_LIMITS; obsolete AuditFull/ReplicaSource -> STATUS_INVALID_PARAMETER/STATUS_NOT_SUPPORTED; plus per-class access (POLICY_VIEW_AUDIT_INFORMATION etc).
LSA policy (security model). Trusted domain query: STATUS_OBJECT_NAME_NOT_FOUND is the standalone-workstation answer (no trusts); add access check on policy handle and *buffer=NULL.
LSA policy (security model). Same as 78 by name: keep STATUS_OBJECT_NAME_NOT_FOUND after the access check; *buffer=NULL.

LSA policy (security model). Returns STATUS_UNSUCCESSFUL. Proposal: Windows signals the event when the policy class changes (audit, domain, server role...). Keep per-class event list in the policy store owner (wineserver or a local LSA service); LsaSetInformationPolicy/rights changes SetEvent() the registered events; invalid class -> STATUS_INVALID_PARAMETER.

Privileges/LSA. Returns STATUS_SUCCESS without removing (fake success). Proposal: remove rights from the per-SID store (28), all=TRUE removes the account; requires admin (POLICY_LOOKUP_NAMES + account DELETE) else STATUS_ACCESS_DENIED; unknown right -> STATUS_NO_SUCH_PRIVILEGE; SID without account -> STATUS_OBJECT_NAME_NOT_FOUND.

LSA secrets/credentials. Returns STATUS_OBJECT_NAME_NOT_FOUND always, so data saved by 87 is never retrievable. Proposal: LSA private data stored encrypted per machine (e.g. in the keyring-backed store SG uses for cred.c, scoped to the machine, not the user); L$ keys readable by the creator, G$ global, M$ machine (admin/SYSTEM only); not found -> STATUS_OBJECT_NAME_NOT_FOUND.

LSA policy (security model). Returns STATUS_UNSUCCESSFUL. Proposal: per-class setters with Windows access checks (POLICY_AUDIT_LOG_ADMIN, POLICY_SET_AUDIT_REQUIREMENTS, POLICY_TRUST_ADMIN...) -> STATUS_ACCESS_DENIED for non-admins; persist PolicyAuditEventsInformation/PolicyDnsDomainInformation etc in the store queried by 77 and signal 80's events; read-only classes -> STATUS_INVALID_PARAMETER.

LSA secrets. Returns STATUS_SUCCESS storing nothing (fake success). Proposal: secret handles from LsaCreateSecret/LsaOpenSecret map to the private-data store of 82/87; set current/old value pair with SECRET_SET_VALUE access check (STATUS_ACCESS_DENIED), STATUS_INVALID_HANDLE for bad handles.

LSA policy (security model). Trusted domain set by name: returns STATUS_SUCCESS doing nothing. Standalone workstation has no trusts -> STATUS_OBJECT_NAME_NOT_FOUND after access check (POLICY_TRUST_ADMIN).
LSA policy (security model). Same as 85 by SID: STATUS_OBJECT_NAME_NOT_FOUND after access check, never success.

LSA secrets/credentials. Returns STATUS_OBJECT_NAME_NOT_FOUND even when storing (PrivateData!=NULL) - it neither stores nor deletes. Proposal: PrivateData!=NULL stores (create/replace) and NULL deletes (STATUS_OBJECT_NAME_NOT_FOUND if absent), into an encrypted machine-scoped store, with Windows prefix rules (G$ global, L$ local, M$ machine: admin/SYSTEM only) and POLICY_CREATE_SECRET access (admin).
LSA policy (security model). Returns STATUS_SUCCESS; acceptable only once 80 exists: remove the (class,event) registration, STATUS_INVALID_PARAMETER/STATUS_NOT_FOUND if not registered.

Credentials. advapi32/tests/cred.c:209-221 ok(): NULL target -> ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER, and no domain creds -> ERROR_NOT_FOUND with count 0/creds NULL - stub matches those. Gap: stored CRED_TYPE_DOMAIN_PASSWORD/CERTIFICATE credentials are never returned. Proposal: search the keyring-backed store (cred.c:456) for domain credentials matching TargetInformation in Windows' order (TargetName, NetbiosServerName, DnsServerName, NetbiosDomainName, DnsDomainName, DnsTreeName, *Session/*.domain wildcards), honour CredTypes/CRED_CACHE_TARGET_INFORMATION; same per-user access as CredRead.

Credentials. CredMarshalCredentialW(BinaryBlobCredential) fails (FIXME) without SetLastError. Proposal (same encoding as UsernameTargetCredential in cred.c): BINARY_BLOB_CREDENTIAL_INFO {cbBlob,pbBlob}: '@@' + char('A'+BinaryBlobCredential) + cred_encode(DWORD cbBlob) + cred_encode(pbBlob,cbBlob); cbBlob==0/pbBlob NULL -> ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER. Tests cred.c:718 leave BinaryBlob as todo (no ground-truth string), so verify round-trip with CredUnmarshal (91) and CredIsMarshaledCredential.

Credentials. CredUnmarshalCredentialW(BinaryBlobCredential) fails without SetLastError. Proposal: inverse of 90: decode DWORD size (6 chars), check len-6 == (size*4+2)/3, allocate BINARY_BLOB_CREDENTIAL_INFO + blob (CredFree-able), else ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER.

SECURITY (SeLockMemoryPrivilege) plus a subsystem (AWE). Windows requires the caller to hold SeLockMemoryPrivilege for AllocateUserPhysicalPages (AWE). Proposal: (1) check the token; if not held -> ERROR_PRIVILEGE_NOT_HELD (honest for normal users). (2) If held: back 'physical pages' with a memfd and track page frame numbers per process; MapUserPhysicalPages mmaps page offsets MAP_FIXED|MAP_SHARED into VirtualAlloc(MEM_PHYSICAL) regions, and FreeUserPhysicalPages unmaps/truncates. Needs a MEM_PHYSICAL region type in ntdll virtual.c.

SECURITY (SeLockMemoryPrivilege) plus a subsystem (AWE). Same design as 317. Also note FreeUserPhysicalPages writes *pages=0 before failing (memory.c:1468), which loses the caller's count. Under the privilege-check step it should leave *pages untouched or set it to pages freed (0) consistently.

SECURITY (SeLockMemoryPrivilege) plus a subsystem (AWE). Same design as 317. BUG: MapUserPhysicalPages does '*pages = 0' (memory.c:1558). Per the AWE contract the page array may be NULL to unmap, so this dereferences NULL, and it otherwise clobbers the caller's PFN array. Fix in any case: never write to pages; with no privilege/AWE return ERROR_PRIVILEGE_NOT_HELD or ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER.

If held and audit policy (LSA) is off, return TRUE (nothing to log, as Windows); when an event-log backend exists, write the record. Route via the ntdll Nt*AuditAlarm syscalls (currently '# @ stub' in ntdll.spec).

SECURITY (ACLs): SetAclInformation returns TRUE and does nothing. Only class AclRevisionInformation is settable on Windows (ACL_REVISION_INFORMATION). Proposal: implement RtlSetInformationAcl (ntdll.spec:1021 '@ stub'): for AclRevisionInformation with len >= sizeof(ACL_REVISION_INFORMATION) set acl->AclRevision (only raising, within MIN/MAX_ACL_REVISION, otherwise ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER). Other classes -> ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER. Too-small len -> ERROR_INSUFFICIENT_BUFFER.

SECURITY (tokens/user profiles): RegOpenUserClassesRoot ignores the token and returns the HKEY_CLASSES_ROOT pseudo-handle (not a real opened key). Proposal: query TokenUser from hToken. If it is the current user, open a real handle to the merged HKCR (RegOpenKeyEx(HKCR,NULL,0,sam)). If it is another user, open HKEY_USERS\\<SID>_Classes (ERROR_FILE_NOT_FOUND / ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED if that hive is not loaded or access is refused). dwOptions != 0 -> ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER. Requires TOKEN_QUERY on the token.
IsInternetESCEnabled: undocumented shlwapi/kernelbase export, untested. Returning FALSE (Enhanced Security Configuration off, the client-SKU default) is plausible, but there is no doc or test.

Missing: what retail ntdll does on a failed assertion (DbgPrint the message and break or prompt when a debugger is attached, versus doing nothing). Only community posts exist, which can't be cited. https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/processthreadsapi/nf-processthreadsapi-getcurrentprocessornumberex: the struct "receives the processor group to which the logical processor is assigned and the number of the logical processor within its group". https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/drivers/ddi/ntifs/nf-ntifs-rtlquerypackageidentity lists STATUS_NOT_FOUND: "A package identity does not exist." Optional extra from the same doc: STATUS_INVALID_PARAMETER when a buffer is given without its size pointer.

Security model. The current code ignores the parent SD, creator SD, token, type and flags, and always returns owner=group=Everyone with world-access DACL and SACL, which is far more permissive than Windows. Proposal per https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/securitybaseapi/nf-securitybaseapi-createprivateobjectsecurityex. Owner/group: creator SD, else parent (SEF_DEFAULT_*_FROM_PARENT), else the token's TokenOwner/TokenPrimaryGroup; validate the owner against the token unless SEF_AVOID_OWNER_CHECK (else STATUS_INVALID_OWNER). DACL: explicit creator ACEs plus inheritable parent ACEs (OI/CI/IO/NP rules; map generic rights via GenericMapping; replace CREATOR OWNER/GROUP; mark INHERITED_ACE; set SE_DACL_AUTO_INHERITED), else the token's default DACL. A SACL needs SeSecurityPrivilege unless SEF_AVOID_PRIVILEGE_CHECK.

Security model. Forwards to RtlNewSecurityObjectEx and drops the GUID list. Proposal: once 368 has a real inheritance engine, make it take the object-type GUID array, so that inherited parent object ACEs whose InheritedObjectType matches any GUID in the array are inherited and others are skipped. Same owner/group/DACL/SACL rules as CreatePrivateObjectSecurityEx (doc URL in 368). No tests in dlls/*/tests.

Security-model API (escalated by rule), but the behaviour already matches. https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/securitybaseapi/nf-securitybaseapi-createprivateobjectsecurityex: "When you have finished using the security descriptor, free it by calling the DestroyPrivateObjectSecurity function" (kernelbase/security.c:982 calls this). Wine frees with the same process-heap allocator RtlNewSecurityObjectEx used. Proposal: keep RtlFreeHeap, demote the FIXME to TRACE, return STATUS_SUCCESS. Nothing else to do.

Security model (ACLs). Returns STATUS_NOT_IMPLEMENTED, so AddAccessAllowedObjectAce (kernelbase/security.c:1430) fails. Proposal per https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/securitybaseapi/nf-securitybaseapi-addaccessallowedobjectace. Append an ACCESS_ALLOWED_OBJECT_ACE: set Flags ACE_OBJECT_TYPE_PRESENT / ACE_INHERITED_OBJECT_TYPE_PRESENT and copy each GUID only when non-NULL. Revision "must be ACL_REVISION_DS. If the DACL's revision level is lower ... changes it to ACL_REVISION_DS". Errors: allotted space exceeded, invalid ACL/SID/flags, revision mismatch. Check that AccessCheck and the wineserver handle object ACEs. No tests.

Security model (ACLs). Returns STATUS_NOT_IMPLEMENTED. Proposal: same layout rules as 371 (doc URL there) with ACCESS_DENIED_OBJECT_ACE_TYPE: GUIDs present only when non-NULL, ACL_REVISION_DS upgrade, same error set. Access checks must honour deny object ACEs, which needs server/token.c review. No tests in dlls/*/tests.

Security model (SACL/auditing). Returns STATUS_NOT_IMPLEMENTED. Proposal: build a SYSTEM_AUDIT_OBJECT_ACE with the GUID-present flags as in 371. OR in SUCCESSFUL_ACCESS_ACE_FLAG / FAILED_ACCESS_ACE_FLAG from the audit bools, matching existing RtlAddAuditAccessAceEx (sec.c:~1440). Use the ACL_REVISION_DS rules. Wine has no audit log, so the ACE is stored only. No tests.

Security model. Returns STATUS_NOT_IMPLEMENTED behind ConvertToAutoInheritPrivateObjectSecurity (kernelbase/security.c:936). Proposal: reuse the 368 inheritance engine. Compute the ACEs the parent would pass down; mark matching ACEs in the current SD as INHERITED_ACE and keep the rest as explicit; set SE_DACL_AUTO_INHERITED/SE_SACL_AUTO_INHERITED; return a new self-relative SD freed by RtlDeleteSecurityObject. No tests in dlls/*/tests.

Security model. Returns *acl=NULL and STATUS_SUCCESS; a NULL DACL grants everyone full access, which is more permissive than Windows. https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/winbase/nf-winbase-createnamedpipea: "The ACLs in the default security descriptor for a named pipe grant full control to the LocalSystem account, administrators, and the creator owner. They also grant read access to members of the Everyone group and the anonymous account." Proposal: allocate (RtlAllocateHeap) an ACL with GENERIC_ALL for S-1-5-18, S-1-5-32-544 and the token owner, and GENERIC_READ for S-1-1-0 and S-1-5-7.

Undocumented SQM/CEIP telemetry export: a search found no learn.microsoft.com page, only CeipIsOptedIn in windowsceip.h. Untested in dlls/*/tests. Missing: any doc for the return value on a session that WinSqmStartSession never really opened. Wine never opts in, so sending no telemetry is the honest model.

Undocumented SQM telemetry (no learn.microsoft.com page) and no test. Returns void; a no-op while not opted in (WinSqmIsOptedIn returns FALSE) is the only plausible behaviour. Missing: a doc. The FIXME could be demoted.

Undocumented, no test. Returns FALSE (not opted in to CEIP). The documented sibling CeipIsOptedIn exists in windowsceip.h, but that page was not fetched, so it isn't cited. Missing: a doc for WinSqmIsOptedIn itself. FALSE is the honest answer because Wine has no SQM consent setting.
Undocumented, no test. Returns INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE (no session). Missing: a doc of the parameters and of the not-opted-in return value.

Undocumented SQM datapoint setter, void return. No doc, no test. A no-op is the only plausible behaviour without telemetry.

ARM64EC-only (signal_arm64ec.c), same as 382. Not built for x86 targets.

The TP_CALLBACK_ENVIRON.ActivationContext field is ignored, so callbacks run without the environment's activation context. The field exists in the SDK struct, but no learn.microsoft.com API documents setting it or its semantics, and no test in ntdll/tests/threadpool.c or kernel32/tests uses it. Missing: a doc or test. Likely fix (unverified): RtlActivateActivationContext around each callback and deactivate afterwards.

The only observable behaviour (returns a usable zeroed DEBUG_BUFFER) passes the tests: ntdll/tests/rtl.c:190 and :205 (buffer != NULL). The event-pair argument and remote-process sections are undocumented. The FIXME is noise and could become TRACE.
Frees the sub-buffers and the buffer and returns STATUS_SUCCESS; tested at ntdll/tests/rtl.c:201 and :213 (ok(!status)). Matches Windows for the tested contract; the FIXME could become TRACE.

Tested parts already match: STATUS_INVALID_CID for a non-process id (ntdll/tests/rtl.c:193); success, InfoClassMask set and non-NULL Heap/ModuleInformation (rtl.c:196-198, 208-210). The documented surface works. https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/synchapi/nf-synchapi-initializecriticalsectionex: Flags "can be 0 or ... CRITICAL_SECTION_NO_DEBUG_INFO", and the single-CPU spin count is forced to 0 (sync.c:251). Tested in kernel32/tests/sync.c:2774-2820 (debug-info behaviour). Wine-internal: reached only when an exception unwinds through host (Linux .so / unix-side) frames via unix_unwind_builtin_dll and finds a host personality routine. No Windows API or counterpart exists; Windows code never runs host-library frames.

Flags 0 and LDR_ADDREF_DLL_PIN work and are tested (ntdll/tests/rtl.c:2280, 2296). The FIXME fires only for other flag bits. Missing: an MS doc of LdrAddRefDll and a Windows test of its result with unknown flags (STATUS_INVALID_PARAMETER vs ignored). Wine headers define only LDR_ADDREF_DLL_PIN (include/winternl.h:4038).

(b) design. The wineserver hands a directory handle's enumeration cache to one client process only (server/change.c:1183-1190). If a duplicated or inherited directory handle is enumerated from a second process, NtQueryDirectoryFile fails with STATUS_SHARING_VIOLATION. On Windows the scan position belongs to the shared file object. Fix needs the enumeration cursor (and ideally the snapshot) moved to the server or a per-file-object shared store. No test covers this.

For files without extended attributes, Windows returns STATUS_NO_EAS_ON_FILE, as tested in ntdll/tests/file.c:5776, 5784, 5794, 5807 (plain ok()). Wine returns exactly that after validating the handle. Wine can never create EAs (NtSetEaFile, item 397), so every file is EA-less and the result is consistent. Full EA support belongs with 397.

(b) design. Always returns STATUS_ACCESS_DENIED, a failure Windows would not give to a writer with FILE_WRITE_EA access. Proposal: store each FILE_FULL_EA_INFORMATION entry as a Linux xattr (e.g. user.wine.ea.<UPPERCASED-NAME> holding flags+value; deleting = zero-length value). Check FILE_WRITE_EA access and validate the buffer (STATUS_EA_LIST_INCONSISTENT); make NtQueryEaFile and NtCreateFile's EaBuffer use the same store; return STATUS_EAS_NOT_SUPPORTED where the filesystem lacks xattrs. No tests exist for Set.

Legacy NT syscall in which the caller supplies the CONTEXT and INITIAL_TEB (its own stack). Not documented on learn.microsoft.com and not called by any test in dlls/*/tests. Missing: a doc or test. A possible design (unverified): map onto NtCreateThreadEx using the start address from ctx (Rip/Eip) and the caller's stack from INITIAL_TEB, which needs custom-stack support in the thread-start path. Rarely used (some packers and injectors).

Resumes the thread but never sets the kernel alert state. Wine has no per-thread alert flag: alertable NtWaitFor*/NtDelayExecution only return STATUS_USER_APC, never STATUS_ALERTED. NtAlertResumeThread is undocumented on learn.microsoft.com and no dlls/*/tests file calls it (grep NtAlertResumeThread: no hits). Only NtAlertThreadByThreadId is tested (ntdll/tests/sync.c:763-833), and that is a different mechanism. Doing this properly needs a wineserver thread "alerted" bit, shared with NtAlertThread.

Returns STATUS_NOT_IMPLEMENTED. NtAlertThread is undocumented in the Win32 docs and has no test in dlls/*/tests (grep: no hits; only NtTestAlert kernel32/tests/sync.c:2899 and NtAlertThreadByThreadId ntdll/tests/sync.c:763 are tested). Doing it properly means a server-side per-thread alerted flag that wakes an alertable wait with STATUS_ALERTED and that NtTestAlert clears. That is not small and there is no ground truth for the exact semantics.

The FIXME is only in the #else fallback for platforms other than Linux/FreeBSD (thread.c ~1947-1950). On Linux the function reads /proc/<pid>/task/<tid>/stat and computes kernel/user times. It is an internal helper, not an API gap on our platform.

Windows docs allow this: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/winbase/nf-winbase-setupcomm says "The device driver receives the recommended buffer sizes, but is free to use any input and output (I/O) buffering scheme ... the function can succeed even though the driver does not allocate a buffer". Linux tty buffers are kernel-managed. Test: kernel32/tests/comm.c:820 SetupComm(hcom,1024,1024).

This stub is the #else of #ifdef __aarch64__ / linux (system.c:1747-1808). It is an ARM64-only SMBIOS core-ID helper and is unreachable on x86_64 builds.

Implemented for the classes the tests cover: SystemProcessorIdleCycleTimeInformation, SystemLogicalProcessorInformationEx, SystemCpuSetInformation, SystemSupportedProcessorArchitectures (ntdll/tests/info.c:1247-1529, 4066-4076; ntdll/tests/wow64.c:154-348). Which other classes the Ex call accepts, and what it returns for them, is neither documented on learn.microsoft.com nor tested.

Fakes success for every class. Only the length check for SystemTimeAdjustmentInformation is real. Test ntdll/tests/info.c:1120 ok(status==STATUS_SUCCESS||status==STATUS_PRIVILEGE_NOT_HELD); info.c:1122,1124 check the length. https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/sysinfoapi/nf-sysinfoapi-setsystemtimeadjustment : "An application must have system-time privilege (the SE_SYSTEMTIME_NAME privilege) for this function to succeed". Proposal: for TimeAdjustment, require SeSystemtimePrivilege enabled (else STATUS_PRIVILEGE_NOT_HELD), then apply via adjtimex() ADJ_TICK/ADJ_FREQUENCY, or fail if the host refuses; never report success for unknown classes (STATUS_INVALID_INFO_CLASS).

Returns STATUS_NOT_IMPLEMENTED. This is the legacy firmware-variable query without a GUID. It has no learn.microsoft.com page (search found none) and no test. It is privilege-gated: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/secauthz/privilege-constants SE_SYSTEM_ENVIRONMENT_NAME "Modify firmware environment values". Proposal: first call the existing check_system_environment_privilege() (system.c ~4290, already used by the Ex variant). Then, on UEFI, either route to NtQuerySystemEnvironmentValueEx with the EFI global-variable GUID or keep STATUS_NOT_IMPLEMENTED, as on BIOS hosts. Owner should decide whether that mapping is honest.

Returns STATUS_DEBUGGER_INACTIVE for all commands. Windows does the same without a kernel debugger: ntdll/tests/info.c:3831 ok(status==STATUS_DEBUGGER_INACTIVE||status==STATUS_ACCESS_DENIED||status==STATUS_INFO_LENGTH_MISMATCH) for every class 0..SysDbgMaxInfoClass with NULL buffers (the wow64 variant is at info.c:3826).

This is the generic #else for platforms other than Linux, Apple and FreeBSD (system.c ~4693-4699). The Linux fill_battery_state (system.c:4473) reads /sys/class/power_supply. The test skips gracefully (ntdll/tests/info.c:1605-1608).

Returns STATUS_NOT_IMPLEMENTED. https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/drivers/ddi/wdm/nf-wdm-zwloaddriver : DriverServiceName is "\Registry\Machine\System\CurrentControlSet\Services\<DriverName>". https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/secauthz/privilege-constants SE_LOAD_DRIVER_NAME "Required to load or unload a device driver". Proposal: check SeLoadDriverPrivilege enabled (STATUS_PRIVILEGE_NOT_HELD); validate the services key (STATUS_OBJECT_NAME_NOT_FOUND); then start the kernel-driver service through services.exe/winedevice, the way Wine already loads drivers, mapping SCM errors to NTSTATUS.

Returns STATUS_NOT_IMPLEMENTED. Counterpart of NtLoadDriver, same privilege (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/secauthz/privilege-constants SE_LOAD_DRIVER_NAME "Required to load or unload a device driver"). Proposal: require SeLoadDriverPrivilege (STATUS_PRIVILEGE_NOT_HELD); resolve the Services\<name> key; stop that driver's service through services.exe/winedevice (SERVICE_CONTROL_STOP); return STATUS_INVALID_DEVICE_REQUEST or the mapped SCM error if it cannot be unloaded. No tests in dlls/*/tests.

Returns STATUS_NOT_IMPLEMENTED. NtRaiseHardError has no learn.microsoft.com page and no test (grep dlls/*/tests: none); nothing in the Wine tree calls it. On Windows it is serviced by csrss hard-error message boxes, and an OptionShutdownSystem response needs SeShutdownPrivilege. Implementing it would mean a hard-error UI path (e.g. user32 MessageBox via a helper) plus a privilege-gated shutdown option; owner decision.

Returns STATUS_NOT_IMPLEMENTED. The native call is undocumented. The Win32 equivalent (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/powrprof/nf-powrprof-setsuspendstate) says "The calling process must have the SE_SHUTDOWN_NAME privilege". Proposal: require SeShutdownPrivilege enabled (STATUS_PRIVILEGE_NOT_HELD); map PowerActionSleep/Hibernate/ShutdownOff/ShutdownReset to systemd-logind Suspend/Hibernate/PowerOff/Reboot over D-Bus; return the failure if logind refuses. Never report success unless the action was accepted.

LPC port subsystem, which is a large design. Windows: ntdll/tests/port.c:387 ok(status==STATUS_SUCCESS) for NtCreatePort(..,100,100,0), or skip on ACCESS_DENIED. Wine skips the whole test (port.c:158 todo_wine win_skip, because NtRequestPort/NtReplyPort are not exported). Proposal: a wineserver "port" object type (named, in the object directory) with connection, message queue and reply semantics, a server_port/client_port pair, and LPC_MESSAGE header handling (32/64-bit layouts as in port.c:60-83). Implement it together with items 421-428.

Part of the LPC subsystem (see NtCreatePort). Windows: ntdll/tests/port.c:242 todo_wine ok(status==STATUS_SUCCESS) for NtConnectPort with SecurityImpersonation QOS. The server then sees an LPC_CONNECTION_REQUEST (port.c:174/180). Needs server-side port objects plus connection handshake; the QOS gives the server impersonation rights, so the security review is part of the design.

LPC connect plus a server-SID check, so it is both security-model and part of the port subsystem. No test in dlls/*/tests. Proposal: implement it as NtConnectPort plus a check that the server port owner's SID equals RequiredServerSid (else STATUS_SERVER_SID_MISMATCH, the Windows status for this case per include/ntstatus.h). Depends on the LPC design (item 420).

Part of the LPC subsystem (item 420). Untested directly. Semantics: block on the server port until an LPC_CONNECTION_REQUEST arrives, which is equivalent to NtReplyWaitReceivePort filtered to connection requests. Implement it with the port object design.

Part of the LPC subsystem. Windows: ntdll/tests/port.c:186 ok(status==STATUS_SUCCESS) for NtAcceptConnectPort(&h,0,msg,1,NULL,NULL), which creates the server-side communication port for the connecting client. Needs the server port design (item 420).
Part of the LPC subsystem. Windows: ntdll/tests/port.c:189 ok(status==STATUS_SUCCESS) after accept. It wakes the client blocked in NtConnectPort. Needs the server port design (item 420).

Part of the LPC subsystem. Windows: ntdll/tests/port.c:246 ok(status==STATUS_SUCCESS) on a connected port handle. Semantics: when the thread exits, an LPC_CLIENT_DIED message is sent on the port. Needs the server port design plus a hook in server thread termination.

Part of the LPC subsystem. Windows: ntdll/tests/port.c:272 and 300 ok(status==STATUS_SUCCESS), reply data matches (273/301), and port.c:274/302 MessageType==LPC_REPLY. Needs the server port message queue (item 420).

Part of the LPC subsystem. Windows: ntdll/tests/port.c:327 todo_wine ok(status==STATUS_SUCCESS). The server loop receives LPC_CONNECTION_REQUEST/LPC_REQUEST/LPC_DATAGRAM (port.c:330-362). Needs the server port design (item 420).

Fake success: returns STATUS_SUCCESS with *handle = 1 (not a real object), so CloseHandle and waits operate on garbage. https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/ktmw32/nf-ktmw32-createtransaction : "Creates a new transaction object" ... "If the last transaction handle is closed before a client calls the CommitTransaction function with the transaction handle, then KTM rolls back the transaction". No tests. Proposal (KTM is a subsystem): a real wineserver transaction object (state active/committed/rolled back, timeout). Transacted registry/file operations (NtCreateKeyTransacted etc.) enlist with it; until those exist, a transaction with no enlistments commits and rolls back trivially and honestly.

Fake success for any handle. With a real transaction object (item 429): validate the handle and type (STATUS_OBJECT_TYPE_MISMATCH / STATUS_INVALID_HANDLE), fail on an already-rolled-back transaction (STATUS_TRANSACTION_ALREADY_ABORTED, include/ntstatus.h), and commit enlisted transacted operations. No tests in dlls/*/tests. Part of the KTM design.

Always returns STATUS_ACCESS_VIOLATION, which is a bogus error, so RollbackTransaction (ktmw32_main.c:79) always fails. With a real transaction object (item 429): validate the handle, mark it aborted, discard enlisted operations, and return STATUS_SUCCESS (STATUS_TRANSACTION_ALREADY_COMMITTED if already committed). Part of the KTM design; no tests.

TokenUIAccess always reports 1 (security.c:600). https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/winnt/ne-winnt-token_information_class : "TokenUIAccess: The buffer receives a DWORD value that is nonzero if the token has the UIAccess flag set." Normal tokens do not have it, and it lets a process bypass UIPI. Security model, no test. Proposal: store a ui_access flag on the server token (default 0; set only through NtSetInformationToken(TokenUIAccess) with SeTcbPrivilege, or for a manifest uiAccess=true signed binary); report that flag with the length checks.

TokenSessionId: validates the length, then reports success without changing anything (fake success). https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/winnt/ne-winnt-token_information_class : "If TokenSessionId is set with SetTokenInformation, the application must have the Act As Part Of the Operating System privilege". Proposal: require SeTcbPrivilege enabled (else STATUS_PRIVILEGE_NOT_HELD); store the session id on the server token so NtQueryInformationToken(TokenSessionId) and new processes see it. No tests.

Returns STATUS_NOT_IMPLEMENTED (kernelbase ImpersonateAnonymousToken, kernelbase/security.c:766). https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/securitybaseapi/nf-securitybaseapi-impersonateanonymoustoken : "enables the specified thread to impersonate the system's anonymous logon token"; it needs THREAD_IMPERSONATE, else ACCESS_DENIED; "Anonymous tokens do not include the Everyone Group SID unless ... (b) Only RSMB is supported, so 'ACPI' and 'FIRM' return STATUS_NOT_IMPLEMENTED (ERROR_INVALID_FUNCTION). learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/sysinfoapi/nf-sysinfoapi-getsystemfirmwaretable lists 'ACPI' ("The ACPI firmware table provider") and 'FIRM' ("raw firmware table provider") as valid providers. The directory is world-readable but the table files are root-only (mode 0400), which is the design decision the owner needs to make.

(b) The Get side of item 853. The doc page above says 'ACPI' "retrieves the contents of the specified ACPI table" (the first table with that name) and 'FIRM' "retrieves the contents of the specified physical address range". On Linux the sources are /sys/firmware/acpi/tables/<SIG> (root-only 0400) and /dev/mem (root-only), so a non-root prefix cannot read them. Proposal: read the table when readable, otherwise keep failing (do not invent tables). The owner must decide whether a privileged helper is acceptable. Unknown providers already match Windows (kernelbase/tests/memory.c:43-44).

SECURITY. Native NtAdjustGroupsToken is also a stub (unix/security.c:854). No test. Doc https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/securitybaseapi/nf-securitybaseapi-adjusttokengroups: needs TOKEN_ADJUST_GROUPS; "cannot disable groups with the SE_GROUP_MANDATORY attribute"; "You cannot enable a group that has the SE_GROUP_USE_FOR_DENY_ONLY"; with a short PreviousState buffer "no group states are changed and the function fails". Proposal: a wineserver adjust_token_groups request implementing these rules, reset restoring SE_GROUP_ENABLED_BY_DEFAULT. The thunk converts TOKEN_GROUPS32 in and out.

SECURITY. The thunk mirrors the 3 classes ntdll supports (IntegrityLevel, SessionId, DefaultDacl). ntdll's TokenSessionId fakes success ("TokenSessionId stub", unix/security.c:762). Doc https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/winnt/ne-winnt-token_information_class: setting TokenSessionId requires "the Act As Part Of the Operating System privilege". Proposal: ntdll returns STATUS_PRIVILEGE_NOT_HELD without SeTcbPrivilege, and otherwise stores the session ID in the server token. Add TokenOwner/TokenPrimaryGroup (SID must be in the token with SE_GROUP_OWNER, else STATUS_INVALID_OWNER), then thunk them with TOKEN_OWNER32/PRIMARY_GROUP32 pointer widening.

(b) WskInspectComplete is only valid on a listening socket with SO_CONDITIONAL_ACCEPT after the app's WskInspectEvent returned WskInspectPend (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/drivers/ddi/wsk/nc-wsk-pfn_wsk_inspect_complete: 'can call ... only on a listening socket that has conditional accept mode enabled'). netio has no event-callback/conditional-accept support (wsk_control_socket is a stub), so this needs the WSK event-callback subsystem. Interim fix: complete the IRP with a failure status instead of returning without completing it.

Unreachable: WskRelease returns WSK_DATA_INDICATION lists that the WSK subsystem only hands to apps through WskReceiveEvent; netio.c never invokes any client event callback (wsk_control_socket, the only way to enable SO_WSK_EVENT_CALLBACK, returns STATUS_NOT_IMPLEMENTED at netio.c:223). Becomes reachable only with the event-callback subsystem (see 1175/1177).

WskSendEx slot: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/drivers/ddi/wsk/ns-wsk-_wsk_provider_connection_dispatch says 'WskSendEx: This member is reserved for system use.' No public prototype (Wine include/ddk/wsk.h:209 notes the same); third-party drivers cannot legitimately call it.

WskReceiveEx slot: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/drivers/ddi/wsk/ns-wsk-_wsk_provider_connection_dispatch says 'WskReceiveEx: This member is reserved for system use.' No public prototype (include/ddk/wsk.h:209); not an API gap for third-party drivers.

https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/drivers/ddi/wdm/nf-wdm-postartnextpowerirp: 'Starting with Windows Vista, the driver is not required to call PoStartNextPowerIrp and a call to this routine does not perform a power management operation.' Wine's no-op matches; downgrade FIXME to TRACE.

(a) Security model: UserMode means the handle must be resolved in the requestor's handle table and checked against its granted access (reject kernel handles, STATUS_ACCESS_DENIED if granted access lacks DesiredAccess, fill HandleInformation). Wine drivers run in winedevice, not in the caller's process, so user handles are foreign. Proposal: for UserMode, duplicate the handle from the IRP requestor process (server get_kernel_object_ptr via client pid), compare NtQueryObject(ObjectBasicInformation).GrantedAccess with DesiredAccess, then kernel_object_from_handle.

(a) Security model: UserMode ObOpenObjectByPointer creates a handle for the requestor with an access check against the object's security descriptor (and honours ACCESS_STATE). Proposal: perform SeAccessCheck-equivalent through wineserver (open with requested access in the client process via get_kernel_object_handle + DuplicateHandle into requestor), never grant more than the SD allows; KernelMode path already implemented.

(a) Security descriptors. https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/drivers/ddi/wdmsec/nf-wdmsec-wdmlibiocreatedevicesecure: 'The security that is applied to the device object is derived from this [SDDL] string unless the system administrator places an override in the section of the registry identified by the DeviceClassGuid'. Proposal: parse SDDL, check HKLM ...\Control\Class\{guid}\Properties overrides, create device via IoCreateDevice, then set the SD on the device's server object (NtSetSecurityObject) so opens are access-checked.

(b) Fakes success with a static stub device (SecuROM hack). https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/drivers/ddi/wdm/nf-wdm-iogetdeviceobjectpointer: returns 'the top object in the named device object's stack and ... the corresponding file object'. Needs resolving device objects that may live in another winedevice process. Proposal: NtOpenFile(name,access); if the device belongs to this process return file object + IoGetRelatedDeviceObject; otherwise a real error, keeping the SecuROM stub only behind an explicit app quirk.

IoReportResourceUsage has no learn.microsoft.com reference page (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/drivers/ddi/ntddk/nf-ntddk-ioreportresourceusage returns 404) and no Wine test calls it. OverrideConflict/ConflictDetected semantics therefore unverified; if implemented, share the claim table proposed for IoReportResourceForDetection (1088).

ExInitializeZone (NT4-era zone allocator) has no current learn.microsoft.com page and no Wine test; ZONE_HEADER layout/semantics cannot be verified from allowed sources. Missing: any Microsoft doc or conformance test for the zone API.

(b) FsRtlRegisterUncProvider registers a network redirector with the Multiple UNC Provider (MUP) so UNC opens are routed to it. Wine has no MUP/UNC-provider routing for kernel redirectors. Proposal: device-manager-side registry of UNC providers; NtCreateFile on \??\UNC\ paths would query registered redirectors (IOCTL_REDIR_QUERY_PATH) before falling back to Samba paths. Large subsystem.

KeQueryPriorityThread: tried in stubs-6. Windows returns the absolute priority (1-31); Wine's NtQueryInformationThread(ThreadBasicInformation) reports the relative THREAD_PRIORITY_* value in Priority and BasePriority (ntdll FIXME 'BasePriority = reply->priority'), so a probe at THREAD_PRIORITY_HIGHEST in a normal process got 2 instead of 10. Proposal: make the server/ntdll report absolute priorities (process class base + relative, with the IDLE/TIME_CRITICAL special values) and then return info.Priority here.

(b) IoRegisterFileSystem inserts a file-system control device into the I/O manager's FS queue for mount processing and notifies IoRegisterFsRegistrationChange callbacks (that export is a spec stub, line 455). Wine has no volume-mount dispatch to kernel file systems. Proposal: maintain FS list + registration-change callbacks in ntoskrnl, and route mount requests (IRP_MN_MOUNT_VOLUME) only once a kernel-FS mount design exists.
(b) Counterpart of IoRegisterFileSystem (1099): removes FS from the mount queue and notifies FS-registration-change callbacks; depends on the same kernel file-system mount design.

(b) Physical memory model. https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/drivers/ddi/wdm/nf-wdm-mmallocatecontiguousmemory: 'allocates a block of nonpaged memory that is contiguous in physical address space'; returns NULL 'If the request cannot be satisfied'. User-space winedevice cannot get physically contiguous memory. Proposal (consistent with Wine's identity MmGetPhysicalAddress): NtAllocateVirtualMemory committed+locked, zero_bits from HighestAcceptableAddress, implement MmFreeContiguousMemory (spec stub 718); document that real DMA is impossible.

(b) Same physical-memory design as MmAllocateContiguousMemory (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/drivers/ddi/wdm/nf-wdm-mmallocatecontiguousmemory). SpecifyCache adds Lowest/Boundary/CacheType constraints that only make sense with real physical pages; proposal as 1101 plus honoring alignment to BoundaryAddressMultiple in VA; MmFreeContiguousMemorySpecifyCache (spec stub 719) needed.

(b) MmAllocatePagesForMdl returns an MDL of unmapped physical pages within a physical range; needs the same physical-memory model as 1101 (allocate locked pages, fill PFN array with identity 'physical' numbers, MappedSystemVa set only by MmMapLockedPagesSpecifyCache). Design decision required, not a stub fill-in.

MmCreateSection is not documented in the WDK reference on learn.microsoft.com and no Wine test calls it; Wine's own prototype (HANDLE *handle first) is unverified against Windows (section object pointer vs handle). Missing: documentation of signature and semantics.

(b) Physical memory model: Windows returns the real physical address of a VA; Wine returns the VA itself (identity). User mode cannot honestly obtain physical addresses without /proc/self/pagemap (needs CAP_SYS_ADMIN). Proposal: decide one model for MmGetPhysicalAddress/MmAllocateContiguousMemory/MmMapIoSpace/MDL PFNs (identity, documented as fake-physical) and keep it consistent; see 1101.

(a)/(b) https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/drivers/ddi/wdm/nf-wdm-mmmapiospace maps 'the given physical address range to nonpaged system space' for device registers; returns NULL 'If space for mapping the range is insufficient'. Real mapping requires /dev/mem (root, CAP_SYS_RAWIO) - a privilege-gated hardware path. Proposal: keep NULL (documented failure) by default; optional admin-gated /dev/mem mmap when Stained Glass runs with that capability, or map Wine's identity 'physical' pages back to their VA for consistency with 1106.

https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/drivers/ddi/ntddk/nf-ntddk-mmlockpagablesectionbyhandle: 'checks to see if the referenced section is resident ... and, if it is, simply increments the reference count'. Wine never pages driver images out, so the section is always resident; the refcount is unobservable to the driver. No-op is equivalent; downgrade FIXME to TRACE.

https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/drivers/ddi/ntddk/nf-ntddk-mmlockpagablesectionbyhandle: MmUnlockPagableImageSection 'decrements the reference count by one'; with a zero count the section merely becomes pageable. Wine never pages driver images, so nothing observable changes; no-op is equivalent; downgrade FIXME.
(b) Counterpart of MmMapIoSpace (1107); behaviour depends on the chosen device-memory mapping design (munmap of a /dev/mem mapping vs no-op for identity mappings).

(a) Security model: UserMode ObReferenceObjectByName must access-check DesiredAccess against the object's SD and honour ObjectType/AccessState; Wine only looks up driver objects in-process (ntoskrnl.c:3060-3071). Proposal: resolve names through wineserver object namespace (NtOpen* by type) with access check in the caller's token for UserMode; KernelMode keeps bypassing checks as on Windows.

(a) Security model: same as ObReferenceObjectByName for UserMode (access check, handle created in requestor context). Proposal: for UserMode open via wineserver with the requestor's token and requested access, failing with STATUS_ACCESS_DENIED as Windows would; also implement RootDirectory (FIXME at ntoskrnl.c:3094).

(a) Paired with ObRegisterCallbacks (1183, security/handle-access filtering). Proposal: free the registration created by a real ObRegisterCallbacks and stop delivering pre/post operation callbacks; today it receives the fake 0xdeadbeaf handle.

ObGetFilterVersion: no learn.microsoft.com page found (wdm/ and ntddk/ nf-*-obgetfilterversion return 404) and no Wine test. Returning OB_FLT_REGISTRATION_VERSION is plausible but unverified. Missing: documentation of the return value.

(a) Tokens/impersonation. PsImpersonateClient makes Thread impersonate Token at ImpersonationLevel. Proposal: map to wineserver thread impersonation (NtSetInformationThread(ThreadImpersonationToken)) on the target thread's handle, obtaining a token handle via ObOpenObjectByPointer(SeTokenObjectType); honour EffectiveOnly/CopyOnOpen by duplicating the token; enforce SeImpersonatePrivilege-equivalent checks as Windows does.

(b) Returns success but never notifies. Process create/exit notifications are system-wide and need wineserver to report every process creation/exit to winedevice. Proposal: server event stream to the device manager, run callbacks in winedevice; bookkeeping: duplicate add -> STATUS_INVALID_PARAMETER, remove unknown -> STATUS_INVALID_PARAMETER (per https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/drivers/ddi/ntddk/nf-ntddk-pssetcreateprocessnotifyroutineex).

(a)+(b) https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/drivers/ddi/ntddk/nf-ntddk-pssetcreateprocessnotifyroutineex: STATUS_ACCESS_DENIED if image lacks IMAGE_DLLCHARACTERISTICS_FORCE_INTEGRITY (code-signing policy); STATUS_INVALID_PARAMETER if already registered or limit reached; callback can veto creation (CreationStatus). Proposal: check the driver image's DllCharacteristics FORCE_INTEGRITY bit, keep table, and deliver PS_CREATE_NOTIFY_INFO from a wineserver process-creation hook before the new process runs.

(b) Returns success but never notifies; thread create/delete notifications are system-wide (all processes). Proposal: wineserver thread-creation/exit events forwarded to the device manager; store up to the Windows limit and call routine(ProcessId, ThreadId, Create).

Each needs per-job state in the server that NtQueryInformationJobObject can read back and, for CPU rate and notification limits, an enforcement (cgroup cpu.max, memory-usage monitoring). Proposal: a set_job_info request keyed by class carrying the structure (validated as Windows does: flags subset, lengths), with CPU rate mapped to a per-job cgroup where the host allows it and a STATUS_NOT_SUPPORTED answer (as DFSS gives, ERROR_NOT_SUPPORTED 50) where it does not; group information validated against the one processor group of this system.

The label lives in mountmgr (volume->label, read from the file .windows-label at the volume's mount root when the volume is created or updated, dlls/mountmgr.sys/device.c:148) and kernel32's SetVolumeLabelW writes that file; mountmgr is not told, so a set through the NT call would be seen only after a rescan. cdrom_DeviceIoControl() takes IOCTL_STORAGE_GET_DEVICE_NUMBER (FILE_DEVICE_MASS_STORAGE) for any handle that has a Unix fd and answers a canned DeviceType FILE_DEVICE_DISK / number 1 / partition 1. Proposal: have the ntdll code return STATUS_NOT_SUPPORTED for IOCTL_STORAGE_GET_DEVICE_NUMBER so that NtDeviceIoControlFile falls through to server_ioctl_file and mountmgr; this could not be verified here (no optical drive or udev in the test environment, so the path is not reachable by a gate).

IOCTL_STORAGE_GET_MEDIA_TYPES(_EX) answers success with DeviceType FILE_DEVICE_CD_ROM and zero DEVICE_MEDIA_INFO entries. https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/drivers/ddi/ntddstor/ni-ntddstor-ioctl_storage_get_media_types_ex requires the array of the media the device supports; the CD-ROM class answer (the supported STORAGE_MEDIA_TYPE values with their DISK_GEOMETRY-like data) is not given on the page and no Wine test covers it. Proposal: answer from the mount manager's device (as for the device number, see CDROM_GetDeviceNumber) which knows the device type and media; not testable without an optical drive.

KeyWriteTimeInformation is accepted and ignored. The registry key's last-write time is kept by the wineserver (struct key: modif) and no request sets it. Proposal: a set_key_info request (key handle, class, value) in the server protocol, for KeyWriteTimeInformation (KEY_SET_VALUE access, sets modif and re-saves the hive) - a protocol change, so every unix module is rebuilt; wow64 passes the LARGE_INTEGER through. Wine has no test for the class.

NtQueryVirtualMemory(MemoryWorkingSetExInformation) answers STATUS_INVALID_INFO_CLASS for another process (the current process reads /proc/self/pagemap). Windows answers per page whether it is in the working set (Valid), shared, share count, protection. Proposal: a new APC type (APC_VIRTUAL_WORKING_SET) so that the target process fills the entries from its own /proc/self/pagemap, the way APC_VIRTUAL_QUERY serves the basic information; the server protocol's apc_call union changes, so it is a protocol bump. A query by page through APC_VIRTUAL_QUERY alone would only tell committed and protection, not residency, and would claim residency for pages that are not.
